newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call down on good liquidity, gilt prices up.
newsitem.headline: Indian call down on good liquidity, gilt prices up.

text.p: Indian call money ended Wednesday below one percent on good liquidity in the banking system while prices of government securities firmed in moderate trade, dealers said.
Call money was traded around one percent for most of Tuesday, with closing quotes around 0.50 percent, they said.

"With liquidity quite good at the moment, it is hard to see any movement in rates beyond the current levels," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "We have to see whether advance tax payments next week will have any impact."
Companies have to make their advance tax payments before December 15.
ICICI Securities and Finance Company (I-Sec) said in a report that it estimated the tax payments at 40 billion rupees. It said it expected call rates to firm up on account of this outflow of funds.
Dealers said prices of governemnt securities firmed up in moderate trade.
"With call money being easy, interest has definitely picked up in government securities," said a dealer. "Although volumes are still not very high, there is definitely more interest in bonds now."

Dealers said the 13.50 percent 1997 government of India stock traded on Tuesday at 102.89 rupees against its last traded price of 102.70. The 12.50 percent 2004 stock firmed up to 94.74 rupees from 94.65, they said.

In shorter-dated securities, treasury bills were in demand, dealers said. Treasury bills maturing in January were traded between 7.0 percent and 7.25 percent. February maturity bills were traded in the 7.25-7.5 percent range while March maturity bills were traded around 7.75 percent, they said.
Dealers said there were no trades in commercial paper or certificates of deposit.
